messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: Mrs. A
Age: 66
Gender: Female
Primary Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
Mrs. A was admitted to the hospital for aphasia evaluation 27 months after onset. The patient had a mild right hemiparesis, right visual field defect, and a severe aphasia. During language testing sessions, she would frequently become frustrated and blocked out reiterating "I don't know." During clinical evaluations, her verbal behavior was replete with echolalic emissions, which increased when anxious and upset. Mrs. A showed significant improvement in language performance when evaluated by her husband.

Summary:
Mrs. A, a 66-year-old woman, was admitted to our hospital for an aphasia evaluation 27 months after suffering a stroke. The stroke resulted in two simultaneous hemorrhagic lesions that affected frontal and parietal areas in the left hemisphere and partially spared perisylvian language areas. Mrs. A had a severe non-fluent aphasia characterized by a markedly reduced spontaneous speech and almost nil auditory comprehension. She also had automatic echolalia, verbal perseverations, and ready-made expressions. Throughout language testing sessions, Mrs. A would become frustrated, blocking out and reiteratively saying "I don't know." Verbal behavior included echolalic emissions that markedly increased when anxious and upset. However, when language evaluation was performed by Mrs. A's husband, her performance improved significantly.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for this admission is the residual severe non-fluent aphasia, a late effect of a left-hemisphere haemorrhagic stroke 27 months earlier, which places it in chapter R. Under ICD-10-AM sequelae conventions the residual deficit is sequenced first and I69 (sequelae of cerebrovascular disease) is added as a secondary code. Aphasia therefore falls under category R47 (speech disturbances).

CODE: R47
